article.title: Opt-out and suppression
article.excerpt: STOP, HELP and START are three different branches. Configuring only the receipt endpoint is the mistake that makes the whole chain fail silently.

p: Keywords are matched on the whole message, case-insensitively, tolerating surrounding punctuation and whitespace. Partial matches do not count.

head: Received
What the platform does
rows: STOP / STOP ALL / UNSUBSCRIBE / CANCEL / END / QUIT / OPTOUT / OPT OUT (also 退订, ABMELDEN)
Adds the number to that tenant's suppression list and sends nothing further of a marketing nature
Replies with a fixed explanation. Does not add the number to any list
Removes the number from the suppression list and replies with a confirmation

steps.p: Configure /webhook/sms/{provider}?token=… in your provider dashboard so delivery results reach the platform.
Configure /webhook/sms/{provider}/inbound?token=… as well. This is the second, separate setting — and the one that is easy to forget.
Reply STOP from a phone, then send a marketing message to that number and confirm it comes back suppressed.
The console lists suppressed numbers and allows a manual release, alongside the automatic START keyword.

sections.scope: Configure only the receipt endpoint and opt-out suppression never triggers. Nothing errors — the chain simply stays silent, which is why this is worth checking first when a STOP appears to do nothing.

sections.h: What the platform will not do for you
p: The gate reads messageType and nothing else. It does not inspect your content.

The inbound token proves which tenant the message belongs to. It does not prove the message genuinely came from that provider — provider signature verification is not implemented. Treat the token as routing, not as authentication.

Not every provider emits an opt-out keyword upstream. Where a provider handles opt-out itself at the carrier level, no inbound event is produced, so our record is a reconciliation aid rather than the only line of defense.

sections.h: Re-subscribing, and why the database being right is not enough
p: Suppression records are not deleted on re-subscribe — the record is closed and the consent history is kept for audit. There is an operator-side console action as well as the START keyword.

Clearing the number on our side only affects our sending. In some cases, including toll-free traffic, the carrier may have blocked the number independently, and the recipient has to take their own action as well. That step cannot be performed by code.
